title: Finite normalization model of the actual pulled-back torsor and its generic fields
statement:
Let $R\hookrightarrow B$ be an injective homomorphism of Noetherian normal domains, let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $E=\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ with the induced inclusion, and let $0\ne f\in R$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $G$ be a finite group, and let $P\to U=\operatorname{Spec}R[1/f]$ be a finite etale surjective $G$-torsor, meaning an action over $U$ simply transitive on every geometric fibre, each of which is nonempty [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Put $U_B=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]$ and $P_B=P\times_U U_B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $P_B$ is a finite etale $G$-torsor. If $T$ is its coordinate $B[1/f]$-algebra, its generic algebra $D=T\otimes_{B[1/f]}E$ admits compatible decompositions
$$\Gamma(P_K,\mathcal O)=\prod_j L_j,\qquad D\cong(\prod_j L_j)\otimes_K E\cong\prod_j(L_j\otimes_K E)\cong\prod_a F_a.$$
Here both index sets are finite and nonempty, $L_j/K$ and $F_a/E$ are finite Galois extensions (finite separable normal field extensions), and $[L_j:K]\mid |G|$. Each $F_a$ is a maximal field quotient of one $L_j\otimes_K E$, with its actual right-hand $E$-algebra structure. The map $T\to D$ is injective, $D$ is the total ring of fractions of $T$ (localization at all nonzerodivisors), and $T$ is normal and integrally closed in $D$. For $C_a$ the integral closure of $B$ in $F_a$ and $C=\prod_a C_a$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], each $C_a$ and $C$ is finite over $B$, and
$$C[1/f]=T\quad\text{as subalgebras of }D.$$
Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}U_B\cong P_B$ over $U_B$, respecting the specified structural maps. No excellence assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Set A=R[1/f], A'=B[1/f], S=Γ(P,O). Finiteness makes P affine and S finite over A. Construct the pulled actions by the pullback universal property and prove geometric simple transitivity by projecting geometric points. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-etale-torsor-section-trivialization] to the diagonal section after self-base-change: its translated-section coproduct is the torsor comparison isomorphism. Faithfully flat affine descent then gives the quotient universal property for each pulled action. Mathlib pullbackSpecIso gives the actual affine tensor presentations with both projections; cancelBaseChange gives the displayed generic pure-tensor comparison.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; actual torsor base-change input

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-field-torsor-galois-components] to $P_K$ and $P_E$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to their finite coproducts. This gives $S\otimes_A K=\prod_jL_j$ and $D=\prod_aF_a$, with their actual field-algebra maps, the asserted Galois properties, and $[L_j:K]\mid |G|$. Both torsors have nonempty geometric fibres over their fields, so neither coproduct is empty. The finite tensor/product comparison is $(l_j)_j\otimes e\mapsto(l_j\otimes e)_j$; its inverse is the sum of the maps from the factors, using their coordinate idempotents. To check the quotient assertion, let $e_j$ be these idempotents in $D$. In a field $F_a$ their images are $0$ or $1$; since they are orthogonal and sum to $1$, exactly one has image $1$. The surjection $D\to F_a$ therefore factors through that $L_j\otimes_K E$, and the resulting map is surjective: an element of $D$ can first be multiplied by $e_j$ without changing its image. Its kernel is maximal. Every map here sends $1\otimes e$ to $e$, so the quotient has exactly the right-hand $E$-structure required in the statement. For the finite affine comparison, reindex Fin n through ULift into the ring universe and apply Mathlib sigmaSpec and its finite-isomorphism instance directly; the projection equations verify the structure map before extracting the algebra equivalence. No separate finite-index sigmaSpec theorem is restated.

source.place: Tags 03SF (section-finite-etale-under-galois) and 03QR (lemma-sheaves-point), field-torsor classification; elementary coordinate-idempotent refinement

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], A' is a normal domain with fraction field E. Etaleness gives flatness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat], so every nonzero base denominator acts injectively [lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain]. The tensor generic algebra D is the localization at the images of these denominators, hence T injects into D. It is finite-dimensional over E and therefore Artinian. A nonzerodivisor of T remains a nonzerodivisor after localization, and every nonzerodivisor in an Artinian ring is a unit. Enlarging the denominator submonoid therefore identifies D with the total ring of fractions of T.

source.place: lemma-flat-torsion-free, immediately before Tag 0539; Algebra Tag 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain); explicit fraction argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal] to $A'\to T$, with the normality of $A'$ from step 3. Thus $T$ is a normal ring, even when it has several components. By [lem-weil-pbc-normal-ring-integrally-closed-total], it is integrally closed in its total ring of fractions. Step 3 identifies that ring, through the actual inclusion of $T$, with $D$. Consequently every element of $D$ integral over $T$ lies in $T$.

For each $a$, $F_a/E$ is finite separable by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-normal-separable-integral-closure-finite] with base $B$, fraction field $E$ and extension $F_a$. Its hypotheses hold because $B$ is a Noetherian normal domain. It gives that $C_a$ is finite over $B$, without excellence. The finite product $C=\prod_aC_a$ is also a finite $B$-module: the coordinate inclusions of finite generating sets generate it. Inside $D=\prod_aF_a$, this $C$ is the integral closure of $B$: an integral tuple has integral coordinates by projecting its monic equation; conversely, choose a monic polynomial over $B$ killing each coordinate, and the product of these finitely many monic polynomials kills the tuple.

Finite T over A' makes every t integral over A' [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. The denominator-clearing lemma for integral elements of a localization supplies one power of f making its entire image tuple B-integral, hence integral in each coordinate. Conversely, if x f^k is a tuple of integral coordinates, multiplying their monic equations shows that the tuple is B-integral. It is A'-integral; multiplying by the unit f^(-k) shows x is A'-integral and thus T-integral in D. Step 4 gives x in T. This proves the stated literal image equality, including a common denominator.

Map A'⊗_B C to the product of the fields by multiplication. It is injective because it is a localization and its restriction to C is the injective coordinatewise inclusion. Tensor induction shows its image is A'-integral and thus lies in T by step 4. The common-denominator equality of step 6 proves surjectivity onto T: x=c/f^k is the image of f^(-k)⊗c. The resulting A'-algebra equivalence, tensor commutativity and Mathlib pullbackSpecIso give the final spectrum isomorphism. The algebra-equivalence commutes equation verifies its structural map.
